sections.h2: Where do you file a deed for Gladwin County land?
sections.html:
At the Register of Deeds in the county building at 401 West Cedar Avenue in the city of Gladwin, the same address as the commission chambers. The office keeps weekday hours from half past eight until half past four.

Each extra instrument assigned or discharged$3, added to the flat fee

Source: Gladwin County Register of Deeds, which points readers to MCL 600.2567 for questions. The flat charge already covers the state's remonumentation and automation shares.

sections.h2: Does Gladwin County offer online land records?
sections.html:
Yes. The register's page links an online land records search and a free fraud alert sign-up, and it says the office takes electronic recording through three vendors. Paper filings still come in by hand or mail.

The office also handles passports, which have nothing to do with land. New applications are taken by appointment, renewal forms are on hand, and photos cost $10. Call before a trip that combines a deed and a passport.

An alert suits any owner who lives elsewhere. The 2020 census counted 16,862 housing units in Gladwin County, of which 34.7% were vacant, and an owner who is rarely on site is the last to notice a paper recorded against the parcel.

sections.h2: What does the state ask a seller to pay at recording?
sections.html:
Mainly transfer tax. The seller owes two levies that together equal $4.30 on every $500 of price: $3.75 to the state and 55 cents to the county, the rate for counties under two million people. A $100,000 sale therefore costs $860. The money goes to the county treasurer within 15 days after delivery of the deed.

The deed carries its value in the text, or an affidavit does. Gifts to a child or grandchild, foreclosure deeds and mortgages fall outside the state levy. Electronic filings may be paid for within one business day of receipt, and all other documents must be paid for when left at the counter.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Gladwin?
sections.html:
Gladwin is a rural, low-density county in the middle of the Lower Peninsula with 26,077 people in the 2025 estimate. It was set off in 1831 and organized in 1875, and its name honors the British commandant at Detroit during Pontiac's War in 1763.

Of its 516 square miles, 502 are land, and nearly all of the Tittabawassee River's flow begins inside its borders. M-18 follows the west side and links the cities of Gladwin and Beaverton, M-30 cuts through the center, and M-61 crosses from east to west through Gladwin and White Star. Ogemaw, Arenac, Bay, Midland, Clare, Isabella and Roscommon counties border it. Local government is two cities and 15 townships.

  • Housing: 17,329 units and 11,280 households, with 86.1% occupied by their owners.
  • Home values: a midpoint of $162,300, with median gross rent of $690.
  • Age: 28.9% of residents are 65 or older.
  • Income: $55,349 for the median household.
  • Permits: 93 building permits in 2025.

Figures: Census QuickFacts.

sections.h2: How did Gladwin County's land come to be settled?
sections.html:
Gladwin's land was surveyed under the Northwest Ordinance in the 1830s, but settlement came much later. The surveyors reportedly doubted the area would ever be settled, and the first census to mention residents was the 1860 count, which listed 14 people, most tied to lumbering camps. County government was organized in 1875.

Population then climbed from 1,127 in 1880 to 4,208 in 1890 and 8,413 in 1910. It reached 19,957 in 1980 and 26,023 in 2000, then eased to 25,386 in 2020. That late, timber-driven pattern means many parcels have a short recorded chain compared with older Michigan counties, though early surveys were not always accurate, and an old legal description can need a corrective survey before a sale.

Land use today is largely rural, with the 2020 census classifying all residents as living in rural areas. Buyers of acreage often ask the register for the full chain, while the equalization department's GIS viewer helps locate the parcel on a map.

sections.h2: How does Gladwin County's tax calendar touch a sale?
sections.html:
Township and city treasurers bill and collect first. The county treasurer's page lists summer bills going out on July 1 and due without interest by September 14, with a different summer schedule for Gladwin City, and winter bills going out December 1 and due by February 14.

On March 1 the unpaid remainder moves to the county, which adds a 4% fee and 1% interest every month. The county's own timeline then shows a $15 mailing fee in October, forfeiture on the next March 1, a personal visit fee, a publication fee in the fall and a last payment date of March 31. Foreclosed parcels go to auction at tax-sale.info. The office does not honor postmarks: the date of payment is the day the county receives and processes it.

The treasurer also certifies deeds, plat maps and tax histories, so order a payoff and history before a sale. For principal residence, taxable value, hardship and veteran questions, the page points owners to the township or city assessor.

sections.h2: Who checks assessments in Gladwin County?
sections.html:
The county equalization department does. It reviews local assessments for the Board of Commissioners and is responsible for keeping each property class in each local unit between 49% and 50% of true cash value, based on an annual study. The local assessor stays responsible for fairness between individual parcels.

  • April: equalization report of values.
  • June: millage reduction fractions for each taxing authority.
  • October: apportionment report of allowable millage rates.
  • December 31: the sales and appraisal study.

The department also maintains the countywide database of values, descriptions, title changes, owner addresses and exemption status, plus a GIS viewer for locating land records and principal residence exemption forms. A deed recorded at the register shows up there as a title change, so a buyer should send in a change of address form after closing.

sections.h2: What if tax is still owed when a Gladwin County house sells?
sections.html:
The sale can still close. The title company pays the delinquent amount from the seller's proceeds, using a payoff figure that includes fees and interest to the closing date.

Timing matters because costs step up. Once a parcel forfeits, monthly interest goes from 1% to 1.5% retroactive to the original delinquency date, and a personal visit and publication fee follow. Redemption rights end at the close of business on March 31, so a seller near that date should request the payoff first. A cash purchase as-is can work on a short timeline when repairs or an inheritance are holding up a listing.

faqs.q: What is the flat recording charge at the Gladwin County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document, whether the document runs one page or many. A discharge or assignment that covers several instruments adds $3 for each extra one.

faqs.q: When is the Gladwin County Register of Deeds open?
faqs.a: The office is open weekdays from 8:30 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon at 401 West Cedar Avenue. The listed telephone number is 989-426-7551.

faqs.q: Can I record electronically in Gladwin County?
faqs.a: Yes. The county says it works with three e-recording vendors. Call the office to learn which vendors it uses before you submit anything online.

faqs.q: Who owes the transfer tax on a Gladwin County sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes it. The combined state and county rate is $4.30 per $500 of price, paid to the county treasurer within 15 days after the deed is delivered.

faqs.q: When does overdue Gladwin County tax go to the county?
faqs.a: On March 1 of the year after the bill was issued. The county then adds a 4% fee and 1% interest each month, and the parcel can forfeit a year later.
